This work aimed to compare methods for the formation of complexes of bixin and curcumin with β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) and to evaluate the stability of the complexes formed by these methods and their food applications.
The stoichiometric relationship between curcumin and β-CD was 1:2 and that between bixin and β-CD was 1:1.
Curcumin-β-CD and bixin-β-CD complexes formed by kneading, coprecipitation, and simple mixing were evaluated by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), thermogravimetry analysis (TGA), or nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR-H).
For both curcumin and bixin, the best method of complexation was coprecipitation.
